answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can submit jobs or vote on disputes. If a cluster of new accounts behaves suspiciously, the system can slash their bonds after evidence and an appeal period, while honest agents retain theirs. This makes a sybil swarm costly: the attacker must immobilize real capital for every identity and risks losing it. A pearl rating, oasis marketplace, or atlas registry can help track histories, but the bond—not the name—creates the deterrent.
